modelResponse.episodeSummary: Robert D. Hale, 68M, Ventricular Fibrillation, critical, pulseless
keyECGEvidence: morphology: No organized QRS; coarse fibrillatory waves ~5 Hz
preEventNote: Runs of PVCs then R-on-T preceded onset; 12-lead 8 min prior showed anterior ST elevation
modelResponse.mechanism: Ischemic substrate leading to electrical instability and ventricular fibrillation

rejectedAlternatives.why: No digoxin listed in home medications or infusions; no specific ECG signs of digoxin toxicity

rejectedAlternatives.alternative: Primary Electrical Disorder (e.g., Brugada, Long QT)
rejectedAlternatives.why: No prior history or specific ECG findings suggestive of these syndromes; acute STEMI is a much more likely cause in this context

recommendedActions: Administer Epinephrine 1 mg IV/IO every 3-5 minutes
Administer Amiodarone 300 mg IV/IO bolus, then 150 mg IV/IO if needed
Consider Lidocaine 1-1.5 mg/kg IV/IO if Amiodarone is ineffective or contraindicated
Administer Sodium Bicarbonate 1 g IV/IO if pH remains < 7.1 after initial resuscitation efforts
Re-evaluate for reversible causes (H's and T's) after initial shocks/medications
Prepare for emergent cardiac catheterization if ROSC achieved
uncertainty: Exact timing of symptom onset relative to ECG changes
Presence of other potential contributing factors not captured
